around.headline: FDA raids seize over Rs 1.4 crore in expired, mislabelled food and medicine from Amazon and Instamart dark stores
around.summary: Karnataka's food safety department raided quick-commerce dark stores run by Amazon and Swiggy Instamart across Bengaluru, seizing expired and mislabelled food and medicine worth more than Rs 1.4 crore, per India Today, The Hindu and Deccan Herald. Before you use anything from a same-day grocery or pharmacy delivery, check the expiry date and batch number on the packet yourself rather than trusting the app listing.
around.source: India Today, The Hindu, Deccan Herald

around.headline: Bengaluru nurse accuses radiologist of drugging and raping her at a diagnostic centre
around.summary: A nurse has accused a radiologist of drugging and raping her at a Bengaluru diagnostic centre, with the accused now booked for rape and criminal intimidation, per The Hindu and The New Indian Express. If you're going in alone for a scan or a procedure that involves sedation, it's reasonable to ask for a nurse or attendant to stay in the room and to note staff names beforehand.
around.source: The Hindu, The New Indian Express

around.headline: Bike ban on elevated corridors put on hold, but flyover restrictions still doubling commute times
around.summary: Authorities have paused a planned ban on two-wheelers using Bengaluru's key elevated corridors, even as existing goods-vehicle restrictions on three flyovers continue to cause chaos, with some commuters reporting journeys taking twice as long, per The Times of India and Deccan Herald. Build in extra buffer time if your route runs through one of the restricted flyover stretches.
around.source: The Times of India, Deccan Herald

around.headline: Pink Line inches closer to launch as BMRCL clears rolling stock for Bannerghatta Road corridor
around.summary: BMRCL has received the rolling-stock clearance needed to bring the Bannerghatta Road stretch into service, moving the Pink Line closer to its planned September launch, per Deccan Herald and Construction World. Worth watching if your commute currently detours around that corridor.

around.headline: Karnataka HC orders fix for Kaveri-2.0 glitch that's been blocking property sale-deed registrations
around.summary: The Karnataka High Court has directed authorities to fix a glitch in the Kaveri-2.0 online registration system that has been blocking property sale-deed registrations statewide, per The Times of India. If you have a registration pending, check with your sub-registrar's office before showing up, since the backlog may still be clearing.

around.headline: Indian shares slide as oil nears $100 a barrel
around.summary: Indian equities turned volatile and slid as crude oil prices approached $100 a barrel, per Reuters. A sustained rise at these levels typically feeds into pump prices and transport costs over the following weeks, so it's worth watching if you're budgeting for a two-wheeler or cab-heavy commute.

street_smart.title: You order paracetamol and packaged snacks through a 10-minute grocery delivery app. When they arrive, the snack packet's printed expiry date is illegible and the medicine strip is dated three months past its expiry — like today's Bengaluru raids where the FDA seized over Rs 1.4 crore in expired and mislabelled goods from Amazon and Instamart dark stores. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: India Today, The Hindu, Deccan Herald and Moneycontrol, Sept 8 — Karnataka's food safety department raided quick-commerce dark stores operated by Amazon and Swiggy Instamart in Bengaluru, seizing expired and mislabelled food and medicine worth over Rs 1.4 crore. This quick-commerce/expired-goods mechanism hasn't been used as a street-smart scenario in the last three weeks — the closest recent consumer-rights topics were a landlord's rental-deposit dispute (Sept 1 and Sept 4) and warranty/consumer-court basics (Aug 18), neither about expired or mislabelled goods bought online.
street_smart.situation: Both items are still sealed in their delivery packaging. The app's return window closes in a few hours.

choices.text: Photograph the expired medicine strip and the illegible snack packet clearly showing the batch number and manufacturing/expiry details, request a refund through the app, and separately file a complaint with the National Consumer Helpline (1915 / consumerhelpline.gov.in) or your state's food safety office, attaching the photos.
choices.feedback: Correct. A refund fixes your own loss, but it does nothing to stop the same expired stock from reaching someone else. The photos are your evidence — batch numbers let the food safety department trace exactly which warehouse and stock lot to target, which is precisely how today's Rs 1.4 crore raid got built: from documented complaints, not just returns.

choices.text: Just use the snack since it's probably fine, and only worry about the medicine if you get sick.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Expired medicine can lose potency or, in some cases, break down into harmful compounds — 'probably fine' isn't a standard you'd want to rely on for a fever or infection. And an illegible expiry date on packaged food is itself a labelling violation regardless of how the food looks or tastes; that's the exact mechanism today's raid was built on.

choices.text: Return both items through the app for an instant refund and leave it there.
choices.feedback: Risky. You get your money back, but with no complaint filed outside the platform, there's no regulatory record — the same warehouse can keep shipping expired stock to the next customer, and the platform has no external pressure to fix the root problem beyond processing refunds as they trickle in.

choices.text: Post about it publicly on social media tagging the company, and skip the formal complaint since public shaming usually gets a faster response.
choices.feedback: Risky. A viral post might get you a quick refund or an apology DM, but it creates no enforceable record the way a National Consumer Helpline complaint or an FSSAI report does. Public pressure and a formal complaint aren't mutually exclusive — file the complaint first, then post if you still want to.

takeaways: Photograph expiry dates, batch numbers and manufacturing details before you unpack or discard anything from an online grocery or medicine order — it's your evidence if something's wrong.

File complaints with the National Consumer Helpline (1915 / consumerhelpline.gov.in) or your state's FSSAI office, not just the delivery app — only a regulator can inspect the warehouse and act beyond your one refund.
Never use medicine past its expiry date on the assumption it's 'probably still fine' — potency loss and chemical breakdown aren't visible from the packaging.

quiz.question: Today's FDA raid on Bengaluru quick-commerce dark stores, seizing over Rs 1.4 crore in expired and mislabelled goods, targeted stores run by which two companies?
quiz.why: The stores are 'dark stores' — warehouses that fulfil online orders directly without a walk-in storefront — which is why routine walk-in food inspections often miss them until a targeted raid.

quiz.question: Which Bengaluru Metro line moved closer to launch this week after BMRCL cleared rolling stock for its Bannerghatta Road corridor?
quiz.why: The Pink Line's Bannerghatta Road stretch needed a rolling-stock clearance from BMRCL before trains could run there, which is what came through this week.

quiz.question: The Cauvery Water Management Authority this week directed Karnataka to release water to which neighbouring state for 15 days?
quiz.why: The CWMA enforces water-sharing between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu under the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal's award, and can order releases even in a normal-rainfall year like this one.

quiz.question: What is the minimum age at which an Indian citizen becomes eligible to vote?
quiz.why: India lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 through the 61st Constitutional Amendment in 1988, one of the biggest single expansions of the country's electorate.

quiz.question: Which gas makes up the largest share of Earth's atmosphere by volume?
quiz.why: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the atmosphere by volume, with oxygen a distant second at roughly 21% — it's oxygen we depend on to breathe, but nitrogen we're mostly surrounded by.
